title: Folic acid handling by the human gut: implications for food fortification and supplementation
authors: Patanwala I, King MJ, Barrett DA, Rose J, Jackson R, Hudson M, et al.
population: Adults with a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, allowing portal vein sampling; randomised crossover of oral stable-isotope-labelled folic acid and 5-formyltetrahydrofolate, 500 nmol (220 µg folic acid equivalent)
funder: Supported by the UK Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (grants BB/F014104/1 and BB/FO14457/1).
authorConflicts: None of the authors had a conflict of interest.
result: Fifteen minutes after a physiological dose of labelled folic acid, 80 ± 12% of labelled folate in the hepatic portal vein was unmodified folic acid; after labelled 5-formyl-THF, only 4 ± 18% was unmodified and the rest had been converted to 5-methyl-THF. The authors conclude that the human gut converts reduced dietary folates efficiently to 5-methyl-THF but has limited ability to reduce folic acid, so that the liver, with low and variable DHFR activity, carries the reduction and may saturate under chronic exposure.
